title: KV-COBRA: KV Cache Compression via Co-Optimized Bit-Rank Allocation
summary: KV-COBRA replaces uniform rank and bit-width assignment across attention heads with a per-head allocator that balances low-rank truncation loss against scalar quantization loss and redistributes the bit budget across heads, aided by a Hadamard rotation and attention-KL-ordered SVD bases. It costs a one-time per-model calibration (SVD, head-wise distortion estimation, allocation solve) plus implementation complexity for mixed-rank, mixed-bit kernels; runtime overhead is stated as zero per token. It can fail if the distortion model mispredicts downstream task sensitivity, if the gains concentrate at extreme bit-rates the reader does not need, or if mixed per-head configurations lack efficient kernel support on a single 24 GB GPU.
rationale: The method directly addresses KV-cache memory limits relevant to long-context inference on a single GPU, but it requires calibration and custom per-head rank/bit handling whose real benefit must be validated on the reader's specific models and workloads.
technique: Per-head co-optimized rank and bit-width KV allocation

It costs a one-time per-model calibration (SVD, head-wise distortion estimation, allocation solve) plus implementation complexity for mixed-rank, mixed-bit kernels; runtime overhead is stated as zero per token. It can fail if the distortion model mispredicts downstream task sensitivity, if the gains concentrate at extreme bit-rates the reader does not need, or if mixed per-head configurations lack efficient kernel support on a single 24 GB GPU.
